chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about drinking fresh juice (unfermented grape juice). He said: 'Drink it as long as it has not boiled/fermented; when it boils/ferments, do not drink it.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, what is the boiling/fermentation?' He said: 'The heart.'

key_terms.الْقَلْبُ: The heart, referring to the thick foam or layer that forms on top of fermenting juice

ai.seo_question: What is the sign that grape juice has fermented and is no longer permissible to drink according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the boundary between permissible fresh juice and intoxicants by identifying the 'heart' (qalb)—a dense, foamy layer—as the definitive sign of fermentation. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the onset of intoxication, marked by this physical transformation, renders the beverage haram, linking the sensory experience of the drink directly to its legal status.
